goal: Test whether a lower official FlagEmbedding BGE-M3 head-only learning rate and training score temperature can preserve the base-best/model-card surface while keeping the sparse+ColBERT local gains seen in v63.

fresh_sources_checked.implication: BGE-M3 is a dense+sparse+ColBERT model; a standalone student should preserve all three modes rather than optimize dense-only behavior.
Official M3 unified finetuning trains sparse and ColBERT heads and combines dense, sparse, and ColBERT scores; fusion surface mismatch can hide or exaggerate progress.
The original method uses self-knowledge distillation across retrieval functionalities and large-batch training, so head-only small-data KD is a limited approximation.
For student retrievers, cached large-batch and guide-model losses are plausible alternatives when simple MarginMSE or small head-only KD is too weak.

fresh_sources_checked.source: Beyond Hard Negatives: The Importance of Score Distribution in Knowledge Distillation for Dense Retrieval
fresh_sources_checked.implication: The next data design should preserve teacher score distribution and not only feed top hard negatives, because top-only hard negatives can underrepresent teacher preferences.
Any later public standalone-model claim needs standard benchmark result files and same-task/same-split evidence, not a private diagnostic alone.

interpretation: Lowering the head-only learning rate from v62's 1e-5 to 3e-6 reduced damage on the ColBERT-heavy best surface but did not produce a robust student improvement.

v64a preserved the base-best surface with only +0.000639 best-vs-best nDCG@10 and improved a weaker sparse-heavy surface by +0.010557, which repeats the v63 pattern of localized sparse/ColBERT correction without a strong standalone gain.
v64b's higher training temperature did not help: the best student surface trailed the best base surface by -0.001013 and several high-ColBERT or sparse-heavy weights degraded.
The evidence argues against blindly scaling v62/v64 with more rows or nearby temperatures. The next attempt should redesign the teacher-data distribution and validation loop before using more GPU.

decision.next_action: Build a v65 data-distribution diagnostic before the next training run: inspect teacher score histograms, query-level entropy, positive/negative strata, and held-out coverage; then generate stratified teacher rows that mix positives, hard negatives, middle-score negatives, and easy negatives. Only after this should another official M3 head or broader student run be launched.
